title: The summer touring route and advertising
summary: The boats toured the upper Mississippi and Ohio from town to town, with daytime and moonlight trips sponsored by organizations.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, we just stopped at Easttown one day, like a circus. We'd go to the next town. We'd operate on the upper Mississippi River and the upper Ohio. And go as far as St. Paul on the Mississippi and as far as Pittsburgh on the Ohio. And do that in the summertime. When we got to the terminus, like at St. Paul, we'd stay there about 10 days. Bigger town, Minneapolis, Paul. A million people would be in the two towns. And Pittsburgh is around 600, 700,000. So we'd stay there a longer time. But other towns would just stay one or two days at the most. I would make the same territory over and over all summer long by just going one town the other. It would be about 30 miles apart from town town. And all over 30,000 population in those days. And now they're going across about twice that size. So we would go from town to town day by day and run a day shirt and a night shirt. And go up the next town and do the same thing.
Did you advertise by posters in advance?

Oh, yes. Oh, yes. We had advertised by posters and newspapers. And organizations, too. We'd handle the best organizations in all the towns. It's sponsored mostly for day trips. In fact, we'd have the Teachers College of Wino in Minnesota. And, well, in fact, all the schools in the springtime, we'd get them in the towns. And others would be sponsored by women's organizations mostly. Church organizations and so on. They would go from one town to another during the day and come back and then we'd take the moonlight, which didn't stop any of us. Where would you spend your one? New Orleans, yeah. Always had a boat in New Orleans. The last 57 years, always had a boat here.
